_rule: External research says what the wider ecosystem does. It never overrides own-account analytics; disagreements are recorded.

findings.claim: November is widely framed by Christian writers as a gratitude-and-remembering month (thanking God while still waiting), and church-year planning puts the First Sunday of Advent at the end of November 2026, so week 2026-11-09 sits in the quiet stretch between the Diwali season and Advent.
findings.source: Ken Kalis, 'Looking Ahead to November: Seven Journeys, One Faith' (2026-11-01)

findings.claim: The dominant November gratitude framing is 'gratitude while waiting / gratitude is not denial' — thanksgiving that does not pretend everything is fine.
findings.source: Dr Traci L. Cain, 'November Theme: God Will Fix My Gratitude' (2026-10-31); The Graceful Chapter (2026-11-01)

findings.claim: Unanswered or seemingly unheard prayer is one of the questions Christians struggle with most but rarely ask out loud; commonly taught answers are yes/no/wait and 'trust His timing', and writers warn against treating prayer like a slot machine.
findings.source: Housely, '15 Questions Christians Struggle With but Rarely Ask' (2025-09-15); GotQuestions.org; christianity.org.uk (Andy Bannister)

findings.claim: INFERENCE: our channel has never covered crying without a reason, night-shift work keeping someone from Sunday service, or being unable to enjoy good news — all three are everyday, send-worthy moments that fit the R1 hidden-feeling pattern and none collides with a prior topic.

Short-form sweet spot for engagement remains roughly 30s-2min even as platform length caps keep rising (Reels/Shorts to 3min); audiences reward shorter, and soundless-captioned viewing stays a core pattern.
findings.source: Kapwing short-form statistics 2026 (2026-07-08); Postplanify 2026 stats roundup citing Buffer's 2026 analysis
